## What are AI Agents? 🤖

- **Model** + **Harness** + **Loop**
- Can read and write files and run commands (incl. `git`)
- Run in the terminal / editor / own app / cloud
- Different levels of autonomy / task horizons: from asking before every step to working on their own

## Agents & git

- git ties in *really* nicely with agents
- Let the agent work on its own branch, not on `main`
  - Locally: git worktrees 🌳 (next slide)
- Review: No unknown changes sneaking in
  - `status` / `diff` (local)
  - merge request (online)

::: {.fragment}
:::{.callout-important}
Agents *cannot* take responsibility for code / changes.
:::
:::

## Detour: Worktrees 🌲🌳🌴

With git worktrees, you can have different branches from one repository checked out *at the same time* — each in a different directory

```bash
git worktree add <path>
```

- `<path>` will be automatically checked for a matching branch / commit / tag
  - If none is found one is created

::: {.fragment}

```bash
# Create a new directory *next* to the repository
# either checkout or create a branch my-feature
git worktree add ../my-feature
```

:::

## Example: Claude Code 🧑‍💻

- AI agent by Anthropic
- CLI / VSCode Extension / App / Web
- Adds itself as a co-author when creating a commit

# Demo: Claude Code with a Worktree

## Integrating with Gitlab

- Claude: Pretty powerful *GitHub* integration (out of the box)
  - Direct creation of PRs / MRs
- Different ways this can be done for GitLab
  - Access to [`glab` CLI](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/)
  - [Authentication](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/) (OAuth vs. Token)
  - Local vs. Cloud (Environment Secrets)

## Optional Practical: Claude Code {background-color="black"}

1. Go back to your Terminal in `git-exercise`
2. Have Claude write a README for your repository *in a worktree*
3. While it does so, examine your file system
4. Opt. 1: Merge the changes into your `main`
5. Opt. 2: Have Claude create a MR for you
